title: Air India Plans to Restore Most International Flights as Middle East Tensions Ease
excerpt: CEO Campbell Wilson signals a potential reversal of route cuts imposed since June, as calmer airspace and falling fuel prices improve the economics of long-haul flying.
body:
• Air India CEO Campbell Wilson said in an internal memo that the airline may wind back schedule reductions on international routes as Middle East tensions ease and jet fuel prices decline.
  • The airline had suspended or reduced flights to North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia between June and August 2026 due to airspace restrictions and record fuel costs.
  • Retrofitted Boeing 787 aircraft have boosted customer satisfaction scores by over 70 points, with Net Promoter Scores rising from minus 31 to plus 43.
  • Air India expects to induct eight additional new or retrofitted widebody aircraft this year, including a new Boeing 787-9.

Air India is preparing to restore most of its curtailed international flights by the end of the third quarter of 2026, as easing tensions in the Middle East reopen airspace corridors and bring down jet fuel prices that had made many long-haul routes commercially unviable.

CEO and Managing Director Campbell Wilson laid out the airline's outlook in an internal memo to employees, signaling a potential turning point after months of painful route cuts that reduced Air India's international footprint to its smallest in years.

What Changed

"The violence in the Middle East has subsided, and although there is no assurance that it won't worsen, the calmer climate has made more airspace available, and fuel prices have considerably decreased," Wilson wrote in the memo, portions of which were reported by NDTV and The Hindu BusinessLine. "We might be able to reverse some of the timetable cuts we made in recent months if this trend continues."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=s7ag-dzKjro

The airline had rationalized services on select international routes between June and August, responding to a combination of airspace restrictions linked to the Iran conflict and record-high international jet fuel prices. Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian carriers, imposed during military tensions in 2025, compounded the problem by forcing westbound flights on longer, costlier routes.

Routes That Were Cut

The reductions hit Air India's most important corridors. Delhi-Chicago and Mumbai-New York were temporarily suspended. Delhi-San Francisco was trimmed from 10 weekly flights to seven. Delhi-Toronto dropped from 10 to five through July. In Europe, frequencies to Paris, Milan, and Rome were reduced. Delhi-Shanghai was suspended entirely.

Despite the cuts, Air India maintained more than 1,200 international flights per month across five continents — a point Wilson emphasized to staff.

"Should this trend continue, we may be able to wind back some of the schedule reductions we'd taken in recent months."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

Fleet Upgrades Driving Satisfaction

Wilson's memo also highlighted early results from the airline's widebody retrofit program. The two retrofitted Boeing 787-8 aircraft currently in service have recorded a Net Promoter Score of plus 43, compared with minus 31 on non-retrofitted aircraft — an improvement of over 70 points. Customer satisfaction scores across cabin comfort, ambience, inflight entertainment, and meals have jumped from 2.7 out of five to 4.1.

Another Boeing 787-8 is undergoing retrofit, and eight additional new or refurbished widebody aircraft are expected to enter service this year, including a factory-built Boeing 787-9. By the end of 2026, Air India aims to have nearly 65 percent of its widebody fleet and over half of its international services operating with upgraded cabins.

New Routes and Milestones

Even as it restores suspended services, Air India has expanded selectively. The airline launched four weekly nonstop flights between Mumbai and Tokyo Haneda, supplementing its daily Delhi-Haneda service. Air India Express is set to become the first carrier to operate a direct international flight from the new Navi Mumbai International Airport, with an inaugural Abu Dhabi service next month.

June marked Air India's strongest operational month, with 86 percent on-time performance overall. But the airline continues to face financial headwinds — the Air India group reported losses exceeding ₹22,000 crore for the fiscal year ending March 2026.

What NRI Travelers Should Know

For Indian Americans who rely on Air India's nonstop connections between US cities and India, the restoration of frequencies to San Francisco, Toronto, and eventually Chicago and New York would bring welcome relief. The airline's retrofit program means passengers on key routes are increasingly likely to fly on aircraft with modern seats, entertainment systems, and improved meal service — a marked shift from the experience that drew years of complaints.

Whether the restoration holds depends on the durability of the Middle East ceasefire and fuel price trends. Wilson's memo struck a cautious note: there is "no assurance" the calm will last.
nri_angle: NRI travelers on US-India routes will benefit from restored frequencies to San Francisco, Toronto, Chicago, and New York, with upgraded Boeing 787 cabins.
